newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - July 11.

text.p: THE NATIONAL BUSINESS REVIEW

Maori leader's fine revives hotel fiasco: The conviction of Maori leader Kara Puketapu this week on tax charges may revive the Quality Inns fiasco which directly led to Winston Peters' sacking from the National Party cabinet in 1992. Page 1.

City trends examined: The Lord Mayor of London, Sir Roger Cork, will head a panel of four experts who will brief Auckland's financial and business community on latest trends in one of the world's leading financial capitals later this month. Page 1.
Opposition to super scheme grows: Since details of the Retirement Savings Scheme were released on Monday, it has been plagued by bad publicity. Page 1.

Confidence boost bypasses Coalition: Public confidence in the country's direction shows a dramatic improvement but it hasn't flowed through to popularity for the coalition government, the latest National Business Review-Consultus poll shows. Page 1.
SFO clears Morgan: The Serious Fraud Office this week cleared New Zealand First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan in its report into Aotearoa Television Network. Page 2.

Censor's bill hurts festival: The New Zealand Film Festival organisation has been burdened by $31,000 of charges from the Film and Video Labelling Body and the Office of Film and Literature Classification for obscure films that will be shown once or twice only. Page 3.
TVNZ may face $800,000 bill for old Gloss fight: Television New Zealand's stroppiness over the brand name "Gloss" may cost the company up to $800,000. Page 5.

Taxpayer to finance Peters' growing wine-box legal costs: The taxpayer looks to meet the costs of Treasurer Winston Peters' representation at next year's judicial review of the performance of wine-box commissioner Sir Ronald Davison. Page 10.

New Fletcher Challenge chief broom sweeps discreetly: Reports on Thursday had it that the market was disappointed that the Fletcher Challenge Ltd board had not brought in "new blood" to replace group chief executive Hugh Fletcher when he retires in December. Page 10.
Accountancy firm back in court: Shareholders in the former Legends Bar in Wellington's St George Hotel are taking a counter-suit against the consultancy firm, Price Waterhouse. Page 10.

Maori leader's conviction raises Quality Inns ghost: Maori leader Kara Puketapu was convicted this week on tax charges relating to double-billed payments of money earmarked for Maori training. Page 13.

New treaty poses cost worry to businesses: University of Auckland law professor Jane Kelsey has warned about the obligations businesses would face under the proposed OECD multilateral agreement on investment. Page 14.
THE INDEPENDENT BUSINESS WEEKLY

Aussie Tax Office socks GPG with huge tax demand: Sir Ron Brierley's Guinness Peat Group, along with two other IEL shareholders, has been hit with a A$876 million demand from the Australian Tax Office. Page 1.

Film deals make late debut at winebox: Documents seized by the Official Assignee's office last July in a bankruptcy raid on the home of Auckland financial consultant Chris Kirkham have surfaced during the final minutes of the winebox inquiry. Page 1.
ACC work capacity test declared fit for implementation: Fourteen ACC claimants found by a trial scheme to be fit for work say they would appeal the decision "if the situation were real". Page 2.

Trustees Executors wins contract to run $400m trust: Tower Financial Services subsidiary, Trustees Executors, custodian contract for the $400 million Trust Bank Canterbury Community Trust, beating off global giants State Street and Chase Manhattan. Page 3.
ASB on brink of major managed funds move: ASB Bank is about to launch a suite of eight unit trusts -- thought to be a suite of passive funds, industry resources say. Page 3.

Kiwifruit board ordered to pay rebels $30k: The Kiwifruit Marketing Board has been ordered to pay $30,000 costs to a group of dissident kiwifruit growers challenged the board's plans to market foreign-sourced fruit in New Zealand. Page 3.

IRD fails to claw back crayfish compo: The Taxation Review Authority has ruled that Gray Jamieson does not owe GST on money paid in an out-of-court settlement he reached with the government after it ruined his marron farming business. Page 7.

IRD to chop jobs again: The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) is planning to give another 150 people the chop in the coming months. According to one source, the IRD this time wants to get rid of higher-paid, more experienced staff. Page 8.
Shipley pushes asset sales: State-Owned Engerprises Minister Jenny Shipley says she favours a partial or full float of Government Property Services (GPS). Page 8.
NZ Salmon to quit fish farm: The New Zealand Salmon Company (NZ Salmon) is asking US$2.8 million for its 50 percent share in Aquacultivos, a fresh salmon producer based in Puerto Montt Chile. Page 8.
